title: Paving the Road to Production: Governed Enterprise AI Agents — Harish Gaggar, Credit Karma
talk_summary: A Credit Karma engineer describes an enterprise agent platform: a dev portal that scaffolds each agent repo with shared memory/tracing/PII/context-optimizer frameworks, a centralized MCP gateway for auth and routing, and per-agent tracking/eval tables. The most concrete, copyable wins are a context optimizer that prunes/reranks/dedupes/compresses payloads before the LLM and a standardized per-run eval schema.

takeaways.technique: Pre-LLM context optimizer (select, rerank, dedupe, compress)
takeaways.what_they_do: Before sending a large payload to the model, they select by token limit, rerank for relevance, dedupe, then compress the curated set.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we do select the payload based on the token limit. Then we re-rank that... And then we dedupe that... and then we finally compress this large payload
takeaways.numbers: 24,000 tokens -> 2,400 (90% saving); Slack bot 24,000 -> ~1,500; '70 to 78% token saves' typical

takeaways.what_they_do: Every agent run writes rows to fixed tables: job tracking, ~8 quality checks per run (success, latency, cost, tool accuracy, safety), a 0-1 eval scoreboard, tool invocations, and step-by-step trajectory.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there is a eight quality checks per run... a scoreboard for your given run, which is basically varies between zero to one

takeaways.technique: Centralized MCP gateway for auth + routing
takeaways.what_they_do: All tool calls go through one gateway that authenticates, stores session state in Redis, issues JWT, and routes by namespace to the right MCP server; no direct endpoint access.

takeaways.technique: Ingest-time PII/secret redaction before LLM and stores
takeaways.what_they_do: Classify data types with severity; above ~90% severity, block and redact at the moment of ingestion so secrets never reach LLM, memory DB, tracing, or eval tables.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If your severity is above 90% or so, uh we will block and redact that uh secrets uh immediately

takeaways.technique: Dev-portal scaffolding with shared frameworks baked in
takeaways.what_they_do: A portal generates each agent repo pre-wired with memory, tracing/eval, context optimizer, and PII frameworks plus provisioned identity/DB/secrets, so every agent is consistent.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the dev portal is going to create a repository, which is going to contains not just the agent framework... but is also going to contains your memory framework, your tracking eval framework

takeaways.technique: Classify-then-plan with HITL gate on risky ops
takeaways.what_they_do: Interpret query, classify as read vs write/sensitive, plan in a subgraph, fetch evidence, check policy; read-only auto-executes, sensitive ops wait for human approval, all logged.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if it is a right and sensitive operations, definitely it will go through the HITL process where you wait for an approval
